paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose you are asked to give advice on whether to attend a vocational college or a university, write an essay to state your opinion. You are required to write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：假设您被要求就是否上职业学院或大学提供建议，请写一篇文章来陈述您的意见。您需要写至少 150 字但不超过 200 字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Half of your brain stays alert and prepared for danger when you sleep in a new place, a study has revealed. This phenomenon is often __26__ to as the “first-night-effect”. Researchers from Brown University found that a network in the left hemisphere of the brain “remained more active” than the network in the right side of the brain. Playing sounds into the right ears (stimulating the left hemisphere) of __27__ was more likely to wake them up than if the noises were played into their left ear.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项研究显示，当你在新地方睡觉时，你的一半大脑会保持警觉并为危险做好准备。这种现象通常被称为“首夜效应”。布朗大学的研究人员发现，大脑左半球的网络比右脑的网络“仍然更加活跃”。与向志愿者的左耳播放声音相比，向志愿者的右耳播放声音（刺激左半球）更有可能唤醒他们。

paragraphs.sourceText: It was __28__ observed that the left side of the brain was more active during deep sleep. When the researchers repeated the laboratory experiment on the second and third nights they found the left hemisphere could not be stimulated in the same way during deep sleep. The researchers explained that the study demonstrated when we are in a __29__ environment the brain partly remains alert so that humans can defend themselves against any __30__ danger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 特别观察到，深度睡眠时，左侧大脑更加活跃。当研究人员在第二个和第三个晚上重复实验室实验时，他们发现在深度睡眠期间，左半球无法以相同的方式受到刺激。研究人员解释说，这项研究表明，当我们处于一个新的环境中时，大脑会部分保持警觉，以便人类能够保护自己免受任何潜在的危险。

paragraphs.sourceText: The researchers believe this is the first time that the “first-night-effect” of different brain states has been __31__ in humans. It isn’t, however, the first time it has ever been seen. Some animal __32__ also display this phenomenon. For example, dolphins, as well as other __33__ animals, shut down one hemisphere of the brain when they go to sleep. A previous study noted that dolphins always __34__ control their breathing. Without keeping the brain active while sleeping, they would probably drown. But, as the human study suggest, another reason for dolphins keeping their eyes open during sleep is that they can look out for __35__ while asleep. It also keeps their physiological processes working.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员认为，这是首次在人类身上发现不同大脑状态的“初夜效应”。然而，这并不是第一次出现。一些动物物种也表现出这种现象。例如，海豚和其他海洋动物在入睡时会关闭大脑的一侧半球。之前的一项研究指出，海豚总是有意识地控制自己的呼吸。如果睡觉时大脑不保持活跃，他们很可能会被淹死。但是，正如人类研究表明的那样，海豚在睡眠时睁开眼睛的另一个原因是它们可以在睡觉时留意捕食者。它还使他们的生理过程保持正常运转。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Elite Math Competitions Struggle to Diversify Their Talent Pool
paragraphs.translationZh: 精英数学竞赛努力使人才库多样化

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Interest in elite high school math competitions has grown in recent years, and in light of last summer’s U.S. win at the International Math Olympiad (IMO)---the first for an American team in more than two decades—the trend is likely to continue.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：近年来，人们对精英高中数学竞赛的兴趣与日俱增，鉴于去年夏天美国队在国际数学奥林匹克竞赛 (IMO) 上获胜——这是二十多年来美国队首次获胜——这一趋势可能会持续下去。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. But will such contests, which are overwhelmingly dominated by Asian and white students from middle-class and affluent families, become any more diverse? Many social and cultural factors play roles in determining which promising students get on the path toward international math recognition. But efforts are in place to expose more black, Hispanic, and low-income students to advanced math, in the hope that the demographic pool of high-level contenders will eventually begin to shift and become less exclusive.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 但是，此类竞赛绝大多数由来自中产阶级和富裕家庭的亚裔和白人学生主导，会变得更加多样化吗？许多社会和文化因素在决定哪些有前途的学生走上国际数学认可的道路上发挥着重要作用。但我们正在努力让更多的黑人、西班牙裔和低收入学生接触高等数学，希望高水平竞争者的人口群体最终会开始发生变化，变得不那么排斥。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. “The challenge is if certain types of people are doing something, it’s difficult for other people to break into it,” said Po-Shen Loh, the head coach of last year’s winning U.S. Math Olympiad team. Participation grows through friends and networks and if “you realize that’s how they’re growing, you can start to take action” and bring in other students, he said.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 去年美国数学奥林匹克竞赛获胜队的主教练 Po-Shen Loh 表示：“挑战在于，如果某些类型的人在做某事，其他人就很难闯入。”他说，参与度是通过朋友和网络来增加的，如果“你意识到这就是他们成长的方式，你就可以开始采取行动”并引入其他学生。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Most of the training for advanced-math competitions happens outside the confines of the normal school day. Students attend after-school clubs, summer camps, online forums and classes, and university-based “math circles”, to prepare for the competitions.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 大多数高级数学竞赛的训练都是在正常上课时间之外进行的。学生参加课外俱乐部、夏令营、在线论坛和课程以及大学“数学圈”，为比赛做准备。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. One of the largest feeders for high school math competitions—including those that eventually lead to the IMO—is a middle school program called Math Counts. About 100,000 students around the country participate in the program’s competition series, which culminates in a national game-show-style contest held each May. The most recent one took place last week in Washington, D.C. Students join a team through their schools, which provide a volunteer coach and pay a nominal fee to send students to regional and state competitions. The 224 students who make it to the national competition get an all-expenses- paid trip.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 高中数学竞赛（包括最终进入 IMO 的竞赛）最大的资助者之一是一个名为“数学计数”的中学项目。全国约有 100,000 名学生参加该项目的系列竞赛，最终在每年五月举行的全国游戏节目式竞赛中达到高潮。最近的一次是上周在华盛顿特区举行的。学生们通过学校加入一支球队，学校提供一名志愿者教练，并支付象征性的费用，将学生送去参加地区和州的比赛。参加全国比赛的 224 名学生将获得一次免费旅行。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. Nearly all members of last year’s winning U.S. IMO team took part in Math Counts as middle school students, as did Loh, the coach. “Middle school is an important age because students have enough math capability to solve advanced problems, but they haven’t really decided what they want to do with their lives,” said Loh. “They often get hooked then.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 去年赢得 IMO 的美国队几乎所有成员都以中学生身份参加了 Math Counts，教练 Loh 也是如此。 “中学是一个重要的年龄，因为学生有足够的数学能力来解决高级问题，但他们还没有真正决定自己一生想要做什么，”罗说。 “那时他们经常会上瘾。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G. Another influential feeder for advanced-math students is an online school called Art of Problem Solving, which began about 13 years ago and now has 15,000 users. Students use forums to chat, play games, and solve problems together at no cost, or they can pay a few hundred dollars to take courses with trained teachers. According to Richard Rusczyk, the company founder, the six U.S. team members who competed at the IMO last year collectively took more than 40 courses on the site. Parents of advanced- math students and Math Counts coaches say the children are on the website constantly.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 另一个对高等数学学生有影响力的供给源是一所名为 Art of Problem Solving 的在线学校，该学校大约 13 年前成立，目前拥有 15,000 名用户。学生可以使用论坛免费聊天、玩游戏和解决问题，或者他们可以支付数百美元与经过培训的老师一起学习课程。据公司创始人Richard Rusczyk介绍，去年参加IMO比赛的六名美国队成员总共在该网站上学习了40多门课程。高等数学学生的家长和数学计数教练表示，孩子们经常访问该网站。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. There are also dozens of summer camps—many attached to universities—that aim to prepare elite math students. Some are pricey---a three-week intensive program can cost $4,500 or more—but most offer scholarships. The Math Olympiad Summer Training Program is a three-week math camp held by the Mathematical Association of America that leads straight to the international championship and is free for those who make it. Only about 50 students are invited based on their performance on written tests and at the USA Math Olympiad.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 还有数十个夏令营——许多都附属于大学——旨在培养精英数学学生。有些课程价格昂贵——为期三周的强化课程可能花费 4,500 美元或更多——但大多数都提供奖学金。数学奥林匹克夏季训练计划是由美国数学协会举办的为期三周的数学训练营，该训练营直接通往国际冠军，并且对成功者免费。根据笔试和美国数学奥林匹克竞赛的表现，仅邀请约 50 名学生。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Students in university towns may also have access to another lever for involvement in accelerated math: math circles. In these groups, which came out of an Eastern European tradition of developing young talent, professors teach promising K-12 students advanced mathematics for several hours after school or on weekends. The Los Angeles Math Circle, held at the University of California, Los Angeles, began in 2007 with 20 students and now has more than 250. “These math circles cost nothing, or they’re very cheap for students to get involved in, but you have to know about them,” said Rusczyk. “Most people would love to get students from more underserved populations, but they just can’t get them in the door. Part of it is communication; part of it is transportation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 大学城的学生还可以利用另一个参与加速数学的杠杆：数学圈。在这些源于东欧培养年轻人才的传统的小组中，教授们在放学后或周末用几个小时的时间向有前途的 K-12 学生教授高等数学。洛杉矶数学圈于 2007 年在加州大学洛杉矶分校举办，最初只有 20 名学生，现在已超过 250 名。“这些数学圈不需要任何费用，或者对学生来说参与起来非常便宜，但你必须了解它们，”Rusczyk 说。 “大多数人都希望从服务水平较低的人群中招收学生，但他们就是无法让他们入学。一部分是沟通，一部分是交通。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. It’s no secret in the advanced-math community that diversity is a problem. According to Mark Saul, the director of competitions for the Mathematical Association of America, not a single African-American or Hispanic student---and only a handful of girls---has ever made it to the Math Olympiad team in its 50 years of existence. Many schools simply don’t prioritize academic competitions. “Do you know who we have to beat?” asked Saul. “The football team, the basketball team---that’s our competition for resources, student time, attention, school dollars, parent efforts, school enthusiasm.”
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 在高等数学界，多样性是一个问题，这已不是什么秘密。据美国数学协会竞赛主管马克·索尔 (Mark Saul) 称，在数学奥林匹克竞赛成立 50 年来，没有一个非裔美国学生或西班牙裔学生——只有少数女孩——进入过数学奥林匹克代表队。许多学校根本不重视学术竞赛。 “你知道我们要打败谁吗？”索尔问道。 “足球队、篮球队——这是我们对资源、学生时间、注意力、学校经费、家长努力和学校热情的竞争。”

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Teachers in low-income urban and rural areas with no history of participating in math competitions may not know about advanced-math opportunities like Math Counts—and those who do may not have support or feel trained to lead them.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 没有参加过数学竞赛历史的低收入城市和农村地区的教师可能不知道像 Math Counts 这样的高级数学机会，而那些知道的人可能没有支持或感觉自己受过领导培训。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. But there are initiatives in place to try to get more underrepresented students involved in accelerated math. A New York City-based nonprofit called Bridge to Enter Mathematics runs a residential summer program aimed at getting underserved students，mostly black and Hispanic, working toward math and science careers. The summer after 7th grade, students spend three weeks on a college campus studying advanced math for seven hours a day. Over the next five years, the group helps the students get into other elite summer math programs, high-performing high schools, and eventually college. About 250 students so far have gone through the program, which receives funding from the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 但是，已经采取了一些举措，试图让更多代表性不足的学生参与加速数学。纽约市一家名为“进入数学之桥”的非营利组织开展了一项暑期住宿项目，旨在帮助那些服务不足的学生（主要是黑人和西班牙裔）从事数学和科学职业。七年级后的夏天，学生们在大学校园里度过三个星期，每天学习七个小时的高等数学。在接下来的五年里，该小组帮助学生进入其他精英暑期数学课程、优秀高中，并最终进入大学。迄今为止，已有约 250 名学生参加了该项目，该项目由杰克·肯特·库克基金会资助。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. “If you look at a lot of low-income communities in the United States, there are programs that are serving them, but they’ re primarily centered around ‘Let’s get these kids’ grades up’, and not around ‘Let’s get these kids access to the same kinds of opportunities as more-affluent kids,’” said Daniel Zaharopol, the founder and executive director of the program. “We’re trying to create that pathway.” Students apply to the program directly through their schools. “We want to reach parents who are not plugged into the system,” said Zaharopol.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. “如果你看看美国的许多低收入社区，就会发现有一些项目正在为他们服务，但它们主要围绕‘让我们提高这些孩子的成绩’，而不是‘让我们让这些孩子获得与更富裕的孩子一样的机会’，”该项目的创始人兼执行董事丹尼尔·扎哈罗波尔(Daniel Zaharopol)说。 “我们正在努力创造这条途径。”学生直接通过学校申请该计划。扎哈罗波尔说：“我们希望接触到那些没有接入该系统的父母。”

paragraphs.sourceText: N. In the past few years, Math Counts added two new middle school programs to try to diversify its participant pool---the National Math Club and the Math Video Challenge. Schools or teachers who sign up for the National Math Club receive a kit full of activities and resources, but there’s no special teacher training and no competition attached.
paragraphs.translationZh: N. 在过去的几年里，Math Counts 增加了两个新的中学项目，试图使其参与者群体多样化——国家数学俱乐部和数学视频挑战赛。报名参加国家数学俱乐部的学校或教师会收到一套充满活动和资源的工具包，但没有特殊的教师培训，也没有附带的比赛。

paragraphs.sourceText: O. The Math Video Challenge is a competition, but a collaborative one. Teams of four students make a video illustrating a math problem and its real-world application. After the high-pressure Countdown round at this year’s national Math Counts competition, in which the top 12 students went head to head solving complex problems in rapid fire, the finalists for the Math Video Challenge took the stage to show their videos. The demographics of that group looked quite different from those in the competition round---of the 16 video finalists, 13 were girls and eight were African-American students. The video challenge does not put individual students on the hot seat---so it’s less intimidating by design. It also adds the element of artistic creativity to attract a new pool of students who may not see themselves as “math people”.
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 数学视频挑战赛是一项竞赛，但也是一项协作竞赛。由四名学生组成的小组制作一个视频，展示数学问题及其在现实世界中的应用。在今年全国数学计数竞赛的高压倒计时结束后，前 12 名学生快速解决复杂问题，数学视频挑战赛的决赛入围者上台展示了他们的视频。该群体的人口统计数据看起来与比赛中的群体截然不同——在 16 名视频决赛入围者中，13 名是女孩，8 名是非裔美国学生。视频挑战不会让个别学生陷入困境——因此它的设计不那么令人生畏。它还增加了艺术创造力的元素，以吸引一批可能不认为自己是“数学人”的新学生。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Middle school is a crucial period when students may become keenly interested in advanced mathematics.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 中学是学生对高等数学产生浓厚兴趣的关键时期。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Elite high school math competitions are attracting more interest throughout the UnitedStates.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 精英高中数学竞赛在全美引起了越来越多的兴趣。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Math circles provide students with access to advanced-math training by universityprofessors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 数学圈为学生提供接受大学教授的高级数学培训的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Students may take advantage of online resources to learn to solve math problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 学生可以利用在线资源来学习解决数学问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The summer program run by a nonprofit organization has helped many underservedstudents learn advanced math.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 非营利组织举办的暑期项目帮助许多服务不足的学生学习高等数学。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Winners of local contests will participate in the national math competition for free.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: We live today indebted to McCardell, Cashin, Hawes, Wilkins, and Maxwell, and other women who liberated American fashion from the confines of Parisian design. Independence came in tying, wrapping, storing, harmonizing, and rationalizing that wardrobe. These designers established the modem dress code, letting playsuits and other active wear outfits suffice for casual clothing, allowing pants to enter the wardrobe, and prizing rationalism and versatility in dress, in contradiction to dressing for an occasion or allotment of the day. Fashion in America was logical and answerable to the will of the women who wore it. Implicitly or explicitly, American fashion addressed a democracy, whereas traditional Paris-based fashion was prescriptive and imposed on women, willing or not.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们今天要感谢 McCardell、Cashin、Hawes、Wilkins 和 Maxwell 以及其他将美国时尚从巴黎设计的束缚中解放出来的女性。独立性来自于对衣柜的系结、包裹、储存、协调和合理化。这些设计师制定了现代着装规范，让连身裤和其他运动服装足以满足休闲服装的需求，允许裤子进入衣柜，并推崇着装的理性主义和多功能性，这与为特定场合或当天的分配而着装相矛盾。美国的时尚是合乎逻辑的，并且服从穿着它的女性的意愿。美国时尚或明或暗地表达了民主，而传统的巴黎时尚则是规定性的，强加于女性，无论她们愿意与否。

paragraphs.sourceText: In an earlier time, American fashion had also followed the dictates of Paris, or even copied and pirated specific French designs. Designer sportswear was not modeled on that of Europe, as “modem art” would later be; it was genuinely invented and developed in America. Its designers were not high-end with supplementary lines. The design objective and the business commitment were to sportswear, and the distinctive traits were problem-solving ingenuity and realistic lifestyle applications. Ease of care was most important: summer dresses and outfits, in particular, were chiefly cotton, readily capable of being washed and pressed at home. Closings were simple, practical, and accessible, as the modem woman depended on no personal maid to dress her. American designers prized resourcefulness and the freedom of women who wore the clothing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 早些时候，美国时尚也遵循巴黎的指令，甚至复制和盗版法国的特定设计。设计师设计的运动装并不像后来的“现代艺术”那样以欧洲为蓝本；它真正是在美国发明和开发的。它的设计师并没有高端的辅助线。设计目标和业务承诺是运动服，其显着特征是解决问题的独创性和现实的生活方式应用。易于护理是最重要的：尤其是夏季连衣裙和套装，主要是棉质的，很容易在家清洗和熨烫。现代女性不需要私人女仆来穿衣，所以款式简单、实用、平易近人。美国设计师珍视穿着这些服装的女性的足智多谋和自由。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many have argued that the women designers of this time were able to project their own clothing values into a new style. Of course, much of this argument in the 1930s-40s was advanced because there was little or no experience in justifying apparel(服装) on the basis of utility. If Paris was cast aside, the tradition of beauty was also to some degree slighted. Designer sportswear would have to be verified by a standard other than that of pure beauty; the emulation of a designer’s life in designer sportswear was a crude version of this relationship. The consumer was ultimately to be mentioned as well, especially by the likes of Dorothy Shaver, who could point to the sales figures at Lord & Taylor.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多人认为，这个时代的女性设计师能够将自己的服装价值观投射到新的风格中。当然，这种论点在 20 世纪 30 年代至 40 年代是很先进的，因为很少有或根本没有根据实用性来证明服装合理性的经验。如果巴黎被抛弃，那么美丽的传统也在某种程度上受到了忽视。设计师设计的运动服必须通过纯美以外的标准来验证；设计师运动装对设计师生活的模仿是这种关系的粗略版本。最终，消费者也被提及，尤其是像 Dorothy Shaver 这样的人，她可以指出 Lord & Taylor 的销售数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: Could utility alone justify the new ideas of the American designers? Fashion is often regarded as a pursuit of beauty, and some cherished fashion’s trivial relationship to the fine arts. What the designers of the American sportswear proved was that fashion is a genuine design art, answering to the demanding needs of service. Of course these practical, insightful designers have determined the course of late twentieth-century fashion. They were the pioneers of gender equity, in their useful, adaptable clothing, which was both made for the masses and capable of self-expression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 仅凭实用性就能证明美国设计师的新想法是合理的吗？时尚常常被视为对美的追求，有些人珍视时尚与美术之间的琐碎关系。美国运动服的设计师们证明，时尚是一种真正的设计艺术，能够满足服务的苛刻需求。当然，这些务实、富有洞察力的设计师决定了二十世纪后期时尚的进程。她们是性别平等的先驱，她们的服装既实用又适应性强，既适合大众，又能够表达自我。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Massive rubbish dumps and sprawling landfills constitute one of the more uncomfortable impacts that humans have on wildlife. They have led some birds to give up on migration. Instead of flying thousands of miles in search of food, they make the waste sites their winter feeding grounds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 大量的垃圾场和庞大的垃圾填埋场是人类对野生动物造成的最不舒服的影响之一。它们导致一些鸟类放弃迁徙。它们不会飞数千英里去寻找食物，而是将废物场作为冬季的觅食地。

paragraphs.sourceText: Researchers in Germany used miniature GPS tags to track the migrations of 70 white storks (鹳) from different sites across Europe and Asia during the first five months of their lives. While many birds travelled along well-known routes to warmer climates, others stopped short and spent the winter on landfills, feeding on food waste, and the multitudes of insects that thrive on the dumps.
paragraphs.translationZh: 德国研究人员使用微型 GPS 标签追踪了 70 只白鹳 (鹳) 在其生命的前五个月内从欧洲和亚洲不同地点的迁徙情况。虽然许多鸟类沿着众所周知的路线飞向气候温暖的地区，但也有一些鸟类短暂停留，在垃圾填埋场过冬，以食物垃圾和垃圾场上繁衍生息的大量昆虫为食。

paragraphs.sourceText: In the short-term, the birds seem to benefit from overwintering(过冬) on rubbish dumps. Andrea Flack of the Max Planck Institute found that birds following traditional migration routes were more likely to die than German storks that flew only as far as northern Morocco, and spent the winter there on rubbish dumps. “For the birds it’s a very convenient way to get food. There are huge clusters of organic waste they can feed on,” said Flack. The meals are not particularly appetising, or even safe. Much of the waste is discarded rotten meat, mixed in with other human debris such as plastic bags and old toys.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从短期来看，鸟类似乎受益于垃圾堆上的过冬。马克斯·普朗克研究所的安德里亚·弗拉克发现，沿着传统迁徙路线的鸟类比只飞到摩洛哥北部并在垃圾堆上过冬的德国鹳更有可能死亡。 “对于鸟类来说，这是一种非常方便的获取食物的方式。它们可以以大量的有机废物为食，”弗莱克说。饭菜不是特别开胃，甚至不安全。大部分废物是丢弃的腐肉，与塑料袋和旧玩具等其他人类残骸混合在一起。

paragraphs.sourceText: “It’s very risky. The birds can easily eat pieces of plastic or rubber bands and they can die,” said Flack. “And we don’t know about the long-term consequences. They might eat something toxic and damage their health. We cannot estimate that yet.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “这非常危险。鸟儿很容易吃掉塑料或橡皮筋碎片，然后就会死亡，”弗莱克说。 “而且我们不知道长期后果。他们可能会吃有毒的东西并损害他们的健康。我们还无法估计。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The scientists tracked white storks from different colonies in Europe and Africa. The Russian, Greek and Polish storks flew as far as South Africa, while those from Spain, Tunisia and Germany flew only as far as the Sahel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 科学家们追踪了来自欧洲和非洲不同栖息地的白鹳。俄罗斯、希腊和波兰的鹳最远飞到南非，而西班牙、突尼斯和德国的鹳只飞到萨赫勒地区。

paragraphs.sourceText: Landfill sites on the Iberian peninsula have long attracted local white storks, but all of the Spanish birds tagged in the study flew across the Sahara desert to the western Sahel. Writing in the journal, the scientists describe how the storks from Germany were clearly affected by the presence of waste sites, with four out of six birds that survived for at least five months overwintering on rubbish dumps in northern Morocco, instead of migrating to the Sahel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 伊比利亚半岛的垃圾填埋场长期以来一直吸引着当地的白鹳，但研究中标记的所有西班牙鸟类都飞越撒哈拉沙漠飞往萨赫勒西部地区。科学家们在期刊中写道，来自德国的鹳鸟如何明显受到废物场存在的影响，六分之四的鹳鸟在摩洛哥北部的垃圾场上存活了至少五个月，而不是迁徙到萨赫勒地区。

paragraphs.sourceText: Flack said it was too early to know whether the benefits of plentiful food outweighed the risks of feeding on landfills. But that’s not the only uncertainty. Migrating birds affect ecosystems both at home and at their winter destinations, and disrupting the traditional routes could have unexpected side effects. White storks feed on locusts (蝗虫) and other insects that can become pests if their numbers get out of hand. “They provide a useful service,” said Flack.
paragraphs.translationZh: 弗拉克表示，现在判断充足食物的好处是否超过在垃圾填埋场进食的风险还为时过早。但这并不是唯一的不确定性。候鸟会影响家乡和冬季目的地的生态系统，而破坏传统路线可能会产生意想不到的副作用。白鹳以蝗虫和其他昆虫为食，如果数量失控，这些昆虫可能会成为害虫。 “他们提供了有用的服务，”弗莱克说。
